title: What is knowledge management?
description: Knowledge management defined, with what ISO 30401 requires of a knowledge management system and how it relates to training and document control.
shortAnswer: Knowledge management is the coordinated set of practices an organisation uses to develop, share, apply, retain and retire the knowledge it needs to operate. ISO 30401, the international standard for knowledge management systems, sets requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, reviewing and improving such a system. It covers people, processes, technology, governance and culture, not only document repositories or search tools.
keyTakeaways: ISO 30401:2018 is the requirements standard for knowledge management systems; a revised edition is at draft international standard stage as at September 2026.
ISO 30401 describes knowledge development as acquisition, application, retention, and handling of outdated or invalid knowledge.
It also describes how knowledge is conveyed and transformed: human interaction, representation, combination, and internalisation and learning.
ISO 9001 separately requires organisations to determine and maintain the knowledge needed to operate processes.
Training is one channel of knowledge management; it depends on the knowledge being accurate and current.

blocks.text: Knowledge management covers how an organisation creates, captures, shares, uses and retires the knowledge its people need to make decisions and do their work. It includes explicit knowledge, such as procedures and records, and tacit knowledge, such as expert judgement.

[ISO 30401:2018](https://www.iso.org/standard/68683.html), published in November 2018 by ISO technical committee 260, sets requirements and provides guidelines for establishing, implementing, maintaining, reviewing and improving an effective management system for knowledge management in organisations. It applies to any organisation regardless of type or size. As at September 2026, a revised edition, [ISO/DIS 30401](https://www.iso.org/standard/89436.html), is at draft international standard ballot and is expected to replace the 2018 edition. Details below reflect the 2018 edition.

sections.heading: What are the components of a knowledge management system under ISO 30401?

blocks.text: ISO 30401 sets out knowledge activities in two groups and expects the organisation to support them with enablers. Practitioners Prieur and Belloni [summarise](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18201) clause 4.4.2 as four knowledge development activities and clause 4.4.3 as activities for conveying and transforming knowledge, which draw on Nonaka and Takeuchi's SECI model.

blocks.caption: ISO 30401:2018 knowledge activities and training implications
head: Activity
What it means
Where training fits
rows: Bringing in new knowledge from inside or outside
Analysing new obligations or methods before content is built
Using knowledge in work and decisions
Practice and assessment on real tasks
Keeping knowledge available when people move on
Capturing expert knowledge in structured form
Identifying and retiring knowledge that is no longer correct
Withdrawing and replacing out of date training
Coaching, supervision, on the job training
Making knowledge explicit in documents, models, media
Frameworks and curricula that connect topics

blocks.text: Around these activities, ISO 30401 uses the common structure of ISO management system standards: context, leadership, planning, support, operation, performance evaluation and improvement. That means a knowledge management system has a policy, assigned roles, documented information, monitoring and a cycle of review, in the same way as a quality or compliance system.

sections.heading: How does knowledge management relate to ISO 9001 organisational knowledge?

blocks.text: [ISO 9001](https://www.iso.org/standard/62085.html) includes a requirement on organisational knowledge (clause 7.1.6 in the 2015 edition), which Prieur and Belloni describe as knowledge "necessary for the operation of its processes and to achieve conformity of products and services". Organisations must determine that knowledge and keep it available. ISO 30401 goes further by specifying a whole management system for knowledge. An organisation certified to ISO 9001 already has part of the foundation, and the new sixth edition, [ISO 9001:2026](https://www.iso.org/standard/88464.html), was published in September 2026.

sections.heading: How is knowledge management different from training or a knowledge base?

blocks.text: Training is one way to convey knowledge to people; knowledge management governs the knowledge itself, including whether it is correct and current. A knowledge base is one tool within knowledge management, used to store and retrieve explicit knowledge.

The distinction matters in regulated organisations because training built on unmanaged knowledge inherits its errors. When procedures change but training does not, the result is [knowledge drift](/glossary/knowledge-drift). A [knowledge graph](/glossary/knowledge-graph) is one technical way to represent how concepts, procedures and obligations relate. For choosing between tools, see [knowledge base vs LMS](/compare/knowledge-base-vs-lms), and for retaining expertise see [capturing subject matter expert knowledge](/guides/how-to-capture-subject-matter-expert-knowledge).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry applies knowledge management principles to training: it defines the concepts, relationships and provenance for a domain first, then generates and assesses learning against that structure. Outdated knowledge can then be traced to every learning element that depends on it.

faqs.a: Yes. ISO 30401 is a requirements standard, so an organisation can be audited against it by a certification body. Certification is voluntary. Organisations should check whether their chosen body is accredited for ISO 30401 and how the upcoming revision will affect transition.

faqs.q: Is knowledge management the same as information management?
faqs.a: No. Information management deals with data and documents as assets: storage, classification, retention and access. Knowledge management also covers how people learn, share expertise and apply judgement. The two overlap in documented knowledge such as procedures.

faqs.q: What is the difference between tacit and explicit knowledge?
faqs.a: Explicit knowledge can be written down, such as a procedure or a rule. Tacit knowledge is held in people's experience and judgement and is harder to express. Knowledge management uses interaction, mentoring and structured capture to make some tacit knowledge explicit and to keep the rest available.

faqs.q: Who owns knowledge management in an organisation?
faqs.a: ISO 30401 expects top management to show leadership and assign roles and responsibilities. In practice, ownership is often shared between a knowledge or information lead, process owners and L&D, with governance defining who approves and retires knowledge.

factCheck.claim: ISO 30401:2018 published 2018-11, ISO/TC 260, stage 90.92 to be revised, 2 amendments; abstract text on scope and applicability.
ISO/DIS 30401 edition 2 is at DIS ballot (stage 40.20) and will replace ISO 30401:2018.

ISO 30401:2018 clause 4.4.2 lists acquisition, application, retention and management of obsolete or non-conforming knowledge; clause 4.4.3 lists human interaction, representation, combination, internalisation and learning, inspired by the SECI model.
ISO 9001:2015 clause 7.1.6 organizational knowledge: knowledge necessary for the operation of its processes and to achieve conformity of products and services.
